structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, then among matched pairs of an oceanic island and a continental area of equal size at similar latitude and climate, the island has far fewer species, and this holds after controlling for climate, latitude and habitat diversity.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Take at least 20 oceanic islands (volcanic or never land-connected, 100–20,000 km² in area). Pair each with a continental window of equal land area, with centroid latitude within ±5° and the same Köppen–Geiger climate class. For birds (class Aves), compute coverage-standardised richness (Chao1 estimate rarefied to equal sample coverage of 0.9, or equal record count). The claim passes if both conditions hold: (a) island richness is lower than its paired continental richness in at least 80% of pairs, and (b) the median island/continent richness ratio is ≤0.50. In addition, in a mixed-effects regression of log richness on log area, absolute latitude, mean annual temperature, mean annual precipitation and an oceanic-island indicator, the island coefficient must be negative with a 95% CI below 0 and a point estimate ≤ log(0.5). The same direction must hold for at least one further class (e.g. Insecta or Plantae) with at least 70% of pairs lower.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim fails if any of the following hold: the island is lower in fewer than 60% of pairs; the median island/continent ratio is >0.75; or the island coefficient in the climate-controlled regression is not significantly negative or has a point estimate above log(0.75). Results between these bounds (ratio 0.50–0.75, or 60–80% of pairs) count as 'not confirmed as far fewer', not as a pass.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'oceanic islands' are mapped to islands that arose from the sea floor and were never connected to a continent (volcanic or coral islands such as Hawaii, Galápagos, Azores, Canaries, Mascarenes, St Helena and Tristan da Cunha). Continental islands (e.g. Britain, Borneo, Madagascar) are excluded. 'Equal size' means equal land area. 'Species of all kinds' means all taxa; the test is run for birds and then repeated for at least one further class. 'Not explained by physical conditions' is operationalised as matching on latitude and climate class and controlling for temperature and precipitation. Modern reinterpretation: this is the island species–area relationship and the island-versus-mainland richness offset, estimated from occurrence records. Raw record counts are biased by observer effort, so richness must be standardised for sampling coverage. Records flagged as introduced (establishmentMeans = INTRODUCED or NATURALISED) must be excluded, because Darwin's claim concerns native species. Records of vagrants, captive animals and fossils must also be excluded.

dataset.name: GBIF Occurrence Data (GBIF.org occurrence search and download service)
dataset.why_it_fits: GBIF offers open occurrence records through its web interface and API. Fields used: taxonKey, scientificName, class, decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude, countryCode, island, islandGroup, establishmentMeans, basisOfRecord, coordinateUncertaintyInMeters, eventDate. Island and continental windows are built from coordinates (with island and countryCode as aids), and area is computed from island polygons. Records with establishmentMeans INTRODUCED, NATURALISED or INVASIVE are dropped, as are fossil and captive records. Richness is then rarefied by sample coverage. Each download receives its own DOI at download time, which should be cited in the analysis; the standing portal has no single fixed DOI.
